chose: The Python ladder has four rungs, each a fact the adapter verifies, and the grade names who enforces it: closure-choked (the interpreter: the protected thing is never a module attribute), checker-choked (Pyright reportPrivateUsage at error over an underscore-prefixed name, or an import-linter contract naming the protected module), reference-choked (Coherence's own check at the edit and in CI, the top rung when neither above holds), convention (underscore prefix or __all__ exclusion alone, enforced by nobody); the TypeScript ladder stays as it is
over: one Python rung, reference-choked, with the underscore prefix and __all__ reported only as evidence
because: the owner asked whether Python can reach TypeScript's security by an analogous route: it can where the interpreter itself prevents import (a name that never becomes a module attribute) or where a checker the project runs refuses private usage, and the ladder should say which enforcer stands behind each rung rather than flatten every Python chokepoint to the rung Coherence alone enforces

chose: The Python adapter never asks Pyright for workspace/symbol; a bare name resolves by a text scan for a definition pattern (def, class, assignment, self.attribute), the component folder first and the whole tree only when the component has no unique non-test hit, then textDocument/documentSymbol on the candidate files
over: workspace/symbol as the TypeScript adapter uses it
because: on PostHog (19,693 source files) one workspace/symbol query took 30 s and pushed Pyright from 350 MB to 3.5 GB because Pyright parses every file to answer it, while a references query costs 3.2 s cold and 0.5 s warm; the text scan reads 23k files in about a second and hands Pyright only the files that can declare the name

chose: The Python adapter indexes the whole workspace and never narrows it: full-workspace enumeration is the only correct option for a Python chokepoint claim, and on PostHog it is affordable (2.2 s to enumerate 19,693 files at 350 MB, 3.2 s for the first references query, about 0.5 s per query warm, 470 MB after a configuration reload)
over: a settings-level python.analysis.include through workspace/configuration (Pyright honors it only when the project has no pyrightconfig.json or pyproject [tool.pyright]; PostHog's pyproject made it log 'No include entries specified' and enumerate all 19,693 files again)

pointing the server at the component folder as its root with the repository as an extra path (0.4 s cold, 160 MB, 1-16 ms per query, but blind to references outside the folder: it missed posthog/caching/test/test_redis_cluster_keys.py's three references to TeamCacheSizeTracker, and a bypass there would have graded the chokepoint clean)

an include list of the component folder plus every file whose text spells a protected name, computed by the adapter (sound, but only reaches Pyright in projects without a config file, and saves half a second per query at the cost of a 23k-file text scan per scope change)
because: Python enforces no visibility, so a reference to the protected thing can sit in any file of the repository; an index that sees less than the whole workspace can only prove the absence of a bypass inside what it sees, and the measured full-workspace cost is seconds and hundreds of megabytes, not the minutes and gigabytes the brief anticipated, once workspace/symbol is avoided

chose: A Python forget reports to Pyright as changed every file the caller names, every file a site landed in, every open document, and every Python file whose modification time moved since the last forget, through workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles
over: reporting only the files the adapter touched, as the TypeScript adapter does
because: Pyright keeps the text of every file it has scanned for an identifier, opened or not, until told it changed, and this client registers no file watcher; the fixture test showed a bypass restored in render.py invisible to the next check because no site had landed there while the file was clean, so the mtime walk (about 0.3 s over PostHog's 23k files) is the safety net for files the caller did not name

chose: A site inside a module's __all__ list classifies as an import (a re-export, no use), and a site in one of a protected package's own files is inside the protected package
over: counting an __all__ entry as a use, which graded a package re-exporting its members broken at module top level
because: Pyright reports the string entries of __all__ as references; an export list brings a name out of the module the way a TypeScript export specifier does, and the check already treats that as an import; and a package's modules are the package, so a reference from pkg/store.py to a member of pkg/ is not a bypass of pkg/

chose: When the Python refutation is vacuous (the instrument did not see the synthetic reference) the chokepoint is graded convention, enforced by nobody, with the verdict not run and the underscore and __all__ evidence in the reason; the ladder carries this as whenVacuous and the TypeScript ladder leaves it unset, keeping its earned grade with not run
over: keeping the earned rung (reference-choked) with the verdict not run, as the TypeScript check does
because: reference-choked names Coherence's own check as the enforcer, and a check whose instrument cannot see a synthetic bypass enforces nothing; what is left standing is exactly the convention, so the grade should say so rather than name an enforcer that is not there; the owner may prefer the TypeScript behavior for both languages

chose: A function-local's refutation is an unsaved edit of its own file adding a use right after the definition, at its indentation, and counts as seen when Pyright reports that site even though it lies inside the chokepoint's body
over: refusing to refute a function-local because no document outside the function can name it
because: the closure rung's whole claim is that the interpreter lets the name be used nowhere else; the refutation proves the instrument reports a use where one is possible, and the account says the site is inside the body and why that is the only place
